speaker: b
text: Where does the process live.

speaker: a
text: `docker-compose.yml` at the root, one service called `deeptutor`, builds from `Dockerfile` target `production`. speaker: b
text: So if I just want the CLI —

speaker: a
text: Separate package, `deeptutor_cli/`. `pyproject.toml` has `[project.scripts] deeptutor = "deeptutor_cli.main:main"`. speaker: b

speaker: a
text: Provider-agnostic, and this is where `deeptutor/tutorbot/providers/` earns its keep. speaker: b

speaker: b

speaker: a

speaker: a
text: Three layers. Layer one — the turn. `AgentLoop` has `context_window_tokens=65_536` as a default, and a builder at `deeptutor/tutorbot/agent/context.py` called `ContextBuilder`. speaker: b

speaker: a

Include detail useful for grep search" — and `memory_update` — "Full updated long-term memory as markdown. Include all existing facts plus new ones. Return unchanged if nothing new." Read that second one again.

speaker: b
text: 記憶 (きおく) — memory layer returns the full markdown, not a diff. It rewrites.

speaker: a
text: Every consolidation is a full rewrite. No CRDT, no patch, no merge. The model is asked for the entire memory file and it replaces the old one. speaker: b

speaker: a

speaker: a
text: Three persistence surfaces. Memory file is markdown on disk — `shared_memory_dir: Path | None` in the `AgentLoop` constructor. Session is SQLite under `data/user/`. Knowledge base is under `data/knowledge_bases/` — you can see the volume mounts in `docker-compose.yml` — and that's where the llama-index vector store sits, chunked PDFs of textbooks, papers, lecture notes. speaker: b
text: Sixth axis — scale.

speaker: a
text: Single container today. The `AgentLoop` has a `TeamManager` with `team_max_workers=5` — that's in-process async concurrency for sub-agent tasks like "grade these five problems in parallel," not horizontal scaling. One uvicorn, one SQLite, one learner comfortably; maybe a classroom if the LLM provider can keep up. Where it breaks: SQLite writes serialize. `SQLiteSessionAdapter.save` does `loop.create_task(self._save_async(session))` — fire-and-forget — which is fine until two channels save the same session simultaneously. For production multi-tenant you'd want Postgres, a queue for the memory consolidator, and probably a per-learner sidecar that pins a long-lived session to avoid cold-starting the context builder every message.

speaker: a
text: One nuance. The load-bearing design choice is the 記憶 file being a single markdown blob that the LLM rewrites end-to-end. It looks naive next to cognee's 図 — diagram — approach, but it's the right call for tutoring because the learner profile is small, grep-searchable, and human-editable. A parent can open the file and read what the tutor thinks about their kid. A graph database gives you better query power at the cost of inspectability, and for an educational tool that a human needs to trust, inspectability beats query power. HKUDS knew what they were optimizing for. That choice is why the learner 能力 が 分かる ようになる — the individual's ability comes to be understood — over a long arc of sessions, without the system becoming a black box.

speaker: b
text: Trust is a load-bearing axis。 信頼 を 守る 為 に、 記憶 を 人間 が 読める 形 で 保存 する — in order to protect trust, store memory in a form humans can read。 それ が 設計 の 核 — that is the core of the design。 親 が 開ける ファイル、 先生 が 直せる ファイル、 学習者 本人 が 削除 できる ファイル — a file the parent can open, a file the teacher can fix, a file the learner themselves can delete。 graph DB だと その 繋がり が 切れる — with a graph DB, that connection breaks。

speaker: a
text: It's load-bearing in every consumer-facing agent, and DeepTutor is one of the first I've seen where the memory layer is designed around the human reader, not just the LLM reader。 人間 が 読める 記憶 は 透明 性 を 生む — human-readable memory produces transparency — 透明 性 は 信頼 を 生む — transparency produces trust — 信頼 は 長 期 使用 を 生む — trust produces long-term use — 長 期 使用 は 個人 の 成長 の 追跡 を 可能 に する — long-term use enables tracking of individual growth。 四 段 論法 だ — it's a four-step argument。 記憶 が 不透明 だと、 この 鎖 が 最初 の 段 で 切れる — if memory is opaque, this chain breaks at the first step。 だから markdown 一 ファイル の 素朴 な 設計 が、 意外 に 深い — so the simple design of one markdown file is surprisingly deep。

speaker: b
text: Next up.

speaker: a
text: Episode thirty-eight — RuView. WiFi channel-state-information pose estimation. You know how a router sees your body as a disruption to its radio signal?

speaker: b
text: 体 (からだ) — body?

speaker: a
text: 体 — body. They reconstruct skeletal pose from WiFi CSI without any camera. Different axis entirely. The LLM axis will be N/A — this is a signal-processing and PyTorch project — and the scaling axis is where it gets interesting because CSI streams are real-time. Compute topology will matter more than context strategy.

speaker: b
text: 楽しみ に なる ようになった — it's come to be something I'm looking forward to。 体 の 動き を wifi で 捉える、 という 発想 は 面白い — the idea of catching body movement via wifi is interesting。 カメラ 無し で 姿勢 を 推定 する — estimate posture without a camera。 プライバシー の 観点 から も 意味 が ある — from a privacy standpoint it also has meaning。

speaker: a
text: 体 の 動き と 脳 の 動き は 繋がって いる — body movement and brain movement are connected — 一方 だけ の 指導 は 不完全 — guidance on only one side is incomplete — 学習 の 未来 は 両方 を 見る tool に ある — the future of learning is in tools that see both。 体 の データ を 個人 の 能力 測定 に 使う 可能性 も ある — there's also a possibility of using body data for individual ability measurement。 運動 の 指導 にも 応用 できる ようになる か も しれない — it might come to be applicable to physical-education guidance too。 DeepTutor が 机 の 上 の 学習 を 支える なら、 RuView は 体 の 学習 を 支える — if DeepTutor supports desk-based learning, RuView supports body-based learning。 対 に なる 二つ の tool — two tools that form a pair。 成長 の 全体 像 を 捉える 為 に は、 記憶 と 体 の 両方 が 要る — in order to capture the whole picture of growth, you need both memory and body。 次 回 を 楽しみ に。

speaker: b
text: 次 回 まで。 体 を 学ぶ、 記憶 を 学ぶ、 両方 を 学ぶ。 Good use. See you next segment.
